title: AP-2 subunit loss converges on a Tfrc-positive, sterol-repressed endocytosis state
exact_observed_result: Ap2m1 and Ap2s1 loss converged on AP-2 dysfunction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, including FDR-supported Tfrc induction under both perturbations and shared repression of Prkcb/Mical2/Kcnn3-like output genes; Ap2s1 also produced a 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut activity/neurotrophin branch with Egr3, Arc, and Vgf repression, and both AP-2 subunits lowered sterol genes in 155 MB Glut.
biological_interpretation: The response is consistent with loss of the AP-2 clathrin adaptor rather than a generic endocytic perturbation: AP2M1 and AP2S1 encode physical AP-2 subunits, transferrin-receptor uptake is known to be AP-2-dependent, and the neuronal mRNA response couples a putative TFRC compensation axis to cell-type-restricted sterol and excitability outputs.

source_findings.summary: Ap2m1 knockdown produced a broad FDR-level downstream signature mainly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with only a small five-gene response in 155 MB Glut.
source_findings.why_it_matters: AP-2 is a core endocytic complex, so the strong restriction of the transcriptional state change nominates a vulnerable neuronal context rather than a ubiquitous scRNA-seq response to AP2M1 depletion.
source_findings.cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
source_findings.main_caveats: Cell-type selectivity is transcriptional only; weaker target engagement and modest cell counts may explain some nonresponsive strata.

source_findings.summary: Vgf, Bdnf, and immediate-early-gene repression identify a recurrent neurotrophin/activity-output marker set after Ap2s1 perturbation, especially in L4/5 cortical and midbrain neurons.
source_findings.why_it_matters: The Vgf signature gives a compact transcriptional biomarker for Ap2s1-sensitive excitatory-neuron physiology that connects endocytosis to plasticity-associated gene expression.
source_findings.cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
source_findings.main_caveats: Vgf is not specific to BDNF, and the report infers reduced neurotrophin/activity output from transcript markers rather than from electrophysiology or BDNF protein.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: 21 cell types; Ap2m1 logFC was negative in all 21, range -0.988 to -0.135; nominal p<0.05 in 16/21; FDR<0.05 in 5/21; perturbed-cell counts ranged from 40 to 181.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: On-target Ap2m1 transcript knockdown across all cell types in which the perturbation was tested.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: 181 perturbed cells versus 23679 controls; 139 genes FDR<0.05, with 48 up and 91 down. Ap2m1 logFC -0.578 FDR 2.41e-08; Gss logFC 0.742 FDR 2.53e-07; Tfrc logFC 0.831 FDR 3.13e-06; Rap1gap logFC -0.337 FDR 9.75e-10; Prkcb logFC -0.592 FDR 4.74e-09; Mical2 logFC -0.706 FDR 8.75e-09; Kcnn3 logFC -0.675 FDR 2.81e-08.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: The dominant Ap2m1 perturbation response occurred in the 151 thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: 144 perturbed cells versus 20353 controls; five genes FDR<0.05. Tfrc logFC 0.964 FDR 1.07e-05; Srebf2 logFC -0.784 FDR 3.64e-05; Ap2m1 logFC -0.590 FDR 1.77e-04; Dhcr24 logFC -0.834 FDR 0.00323; Hap1 logFC -0.679 FDR 0.0321.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: A smaller Ap2m1 response in midbrain glutamatergic cells coupled TFRC induction to Srebf2 and Dhcr24 repression.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: Eleven cell types had nominal Ap2m1 p<0.05 but target FDR>=0.315 and zero FDR<0.05 downstream genes; five cell types lacked nominal Ap2m1 p<0.05 and also had zero FDR<0.05 genes.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: Many null cell-type results coincided with weak or FDR-insignificant Ap2m1 self-statistics.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: 176 Ap2s1 cells versus 15039 controls; Ap2s1 logFC -0.757 FDR 0.00991; 110 genes at FDR<0.05. Egr3 logFC -1.333 FDR 1.35e-13; Srebf2 -0.631 FDR 2.17e-10; Arc -0.893 FDR 2.56e-07; Vgf -0.633 FDR 2.52e-04; Ptprn2 +0.330 FDR 2.64e-05; Mgat5b +0.822 FDR 2.80e-05; Jun +0.843 FDR 1.83e-04.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: Ap2s1 perturbation in L4/5 intratelencephalic cortical excitatory neurons produced a moderate signature with repression of activity-associated transcripts and Srebf2.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: Vgf was negative in 22/23 Ap2s1 cell types and FDR<0.05 in 6/23: 191 MB P MY GABA logFC -1.451 FDR 5.40e-04; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut -0.633 FDR 2.52e-04; 001 L5-6 IT Glut -1.180 FDR 0.00399; 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut -0.792 FDR 0.0220; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut -0.925 FDR 0.0423; 155 MB Glut -1.042 FDR 0.0248. Bdnf was FDR<0.05 and negative in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: A neurotrophin/activity-associated transcriptional marker set was repeatedly reduced after Ap2s1 perturbation.

caveats: Transcriptome data do not measure coated-pit formation, surface TFRC, iron uptake, cholesterol abundance, or neuronal firing.
Several recurrent Tfrc increases outside the largest classes were nominal rather than FDR-significant.

citations.citation: UniProtKB reviewed entries P84091 and Q96CW1 for AP-2 complex subunit mu.
citations.description: Defines AP2M1 as the AP-2 mu subunit, describes AP-2 cargo recognition and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, and lists AP2S1/AP2B1/alpha adaptins as heterotetrameric complex partners.

citations.citation: Reactome pathways R-HSA-8856828 and R-HSA-8856825 for clathrin-mediated endocytosis and cargo recognition for clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
citations.description: Places human AP2M1 in curated clathrin-mediated endocytosis and cargo-recognition pathway contexts.

citations.citation: Motley A, Bright NA, Seaman MNJ, Robinson MS. Clathrin-mediated endocytosis in AP-2-depleted cells. J Cell Biol. 2003;162(5):909-918. doi:10.1083/jcb.200305145.
citations.description: AP-2 mu2 RNAi in HeLaM cells reduced coated pits and severely inhibited receptor-mediated transferrin uptake, establishing TFRC as AP-2-dependent cargo in a perturbation experiment.

citations.citation: Helbig I, Lopez-Hernandez T, Shor O, et al. A Recurrent Missense Variant in AP2M1 Impairs Clathrin-Mediated Endocytosis and Causes Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy. Am J Hum Genet. 2019;104(6):1060-1072. doi:10.1016/j.ajhg.2019.04.001.
citations.description: Links AP2M1 dysfunction to human developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and shows defective transferrin clathrin-mediated endocytosis for the recurrent p.Arg170Trp variant.

citations.citation: Reactome pathways R-HSA-8856828 Clathrin-mediated endocytosis and R-HSA-1655829 Regulation of cholesterol biosynthesis by SREBP (SREBF).
citations.description: Places AP2S1 in clathrin-mediated endocytosis and records the SREBP-regulated cholesterol-biosynthesis pathway used to interpret the Srebf2 module.
